title: Judges 8
paragraphs: ¹ Now the men of Ephraim said to Gideon, "Why have you treated us this way? Why didn't you call us when you went out to fight Midian?" And they sharply rebuked him. ² But he answered them, "What have I accomplished compared to you? Isn't the gleaning of Ephraim's grapes better than the full grape harvest of Abiezer? ³ God gave you Oreb and Zeeb, the leaders of Midian. What was I able to do compared to you?" When he said this, their anger against him subsided. ⁴ Gideon and his three hundred men, exhausted yet still in pursuit, crossed the Jordan. ⁵ He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give my troops some bread; they are worn out, and I'm pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."

⁶ But the leaders of Succoth said, "Do you already have the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your possession? Why should we give bread to your troops?" ⁷ Gideon replied, "Just for that, when the LORD gives me Zebah and Zalmunna, I will thrash your bodies with desert thorns and briers." ⁸ He went up from there to Peniel and made the same request, but the men of Peniel gave him the same answer as the men of Succoth. ⁹ He also said to the men of Peniel, "When I return safely, I will tear down this tower." ¹⁰ Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their forces — about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the armies of the eastern peoples; a hundred and twenty thousand soldiers had already fallen.

¹¹ Gideon went up by the route of the nomads east of Nobah and Jogbehah and attacked the army while they were off guard. ¹² When Zebah and Zalmunna fled, he pursued them, captured both Midianite kings, and threw their entire army into a panic. ¹³ Gideon son of Joash then returned from the battle before the sun was up. ¹⁴ He captured a young man from Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the names of the seventy-seven officials and elders of Succoth. ¹⁵ Then Gideon came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me by saying, 'Do you already have Zebah and Zalmunna in your possession? Why should we give bread to your exhausted men?'"

¹⁶ He took the elders of the city and punished the men of Succoth with desert thorns and briers. ¹⁷ He also tore down the tower of Peniel and killed the men of the city. ¹⁸ Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, "What were the men like that you killed at Tabor?" They answered, "They were men just like you — every one of them looked like the son of a king." ¹⁹ Gideon replied, "Those were my brothers, my own mother's sons. As surely as the LORD lives, if you had spared their lives, I would not kill you." ²⁰ Then he said to his firstborn son Jether, "Draw your sword and kill them." But the boy did not draw his sword, because he was still young and afraid.

²¹ Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Come, kill us yourself. 'As the man is, so is his strength.'" So Gideon stepped forward and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescent ornaments from their camels' necks. ²² The Israelites said to Gideon, "Rule over us — you, your son, and your grandson — because you have saved us from the hand of Midian." ²³ But Gideon told them, "I will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you. The LORD will rule over you." ²⁴ And he said, "I do have one request: each of you give me an earring from your share of the plunder." (It was the custom of the Ishmaelites to wear gold earrings.) ²⁵ "We'll be glad to give them," they answered. So they spread out a garment, and each man threw in an earring from his plunder.

²⁶ The weight of the golden earrings he had requested came to seventeen hundred shekels of gold, not counting the ornaments, pendants, and purple robes worn by the kings of Midian, or the chains around their camels' necks. ²⁷ Gideon made an ephod from this gold and set it up in his city of Ophrah. All Israel prostituted themselves by worshiping it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and his family. ²⁸ So Midian was subdued before the Israelites and no longer raised its head. The land had peace for forty years during Gideon's lifetime. ²⁹ Jerubbaal (Gideon) the son of Joash went back to live in his own house. ³⁰ He had seventy sons of his own, for he had many wives.

³¹ His concubine who lived in Shechem also bore him a son, whom he named Abimelech. ³² Gideon the son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash at Ophrah of the Abiezrites. ³³ As soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites turned back to prostituting themselves with the Baals. They made Baal-Berith their god. ³⁴ The Israelites did not remember the LORD their God, who had rescued them from all their enemies on every side. ³⁵ Nor did they show loyalty to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, in return for all the good he had done for Israel.
